parts:
Hello,

I've been working with the point count example of the Montrave dataset for a couple of days now. Admittedly my experience with R is limited to simple analyses, but I do want to become more proficient with it so I'm trying to learn to analyze VCP data for the first time using the R Distance package instead of the Distance software interface. I am embarrassed by how long it has taken me to work with the example dataset being that you all have provided a link to the code, but nonetheless I have one issue I still cannot figure out. I'm getting an error when running the half-normal key function:

Starting AIC adjustment term selection.
Fitting half-normal key function
Key only models do not require monotonicity contraints. Not constraining model for monotonicity.
AIC= 444.782
Fitting half-normal key function with Hermite(4) adjustments
AIC= 444.524
Fitting half-normal key function with Hermite(4,6) adjustments


Error in model fitting, returning: half-normal key function with Hermite(4) adjustments

  Error: Error in detfct.fit.opt(ddfobj, optim.options, bounds, misc.options) :
  No convergence.

The uniform and hazard-rate key functions worked fine. Is this something I should be worried about? Or, just an additional sign that I do not want to select the half-normal key function? I could not find any mention of this in the Montrave case study document or Buckland et al. 2015, so I'm guessing I may have done something wrong?

Also, the results I get are different from those provided in Table 5.5 in Buckland et al. 2015. Delta AICs for uniform and half-normal compared to hazard-rate are 2.68 and 0.75, respectively and model results are:

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Montrave point dataset error in half-normal key function detection model
parts:
That’s interesting.  I did the Montrave analyses for the book using the Distance software interface.  I was not comfortable with estimation using the half-normal model.  In my analyses, AIC selected one HP adjustment narrowly over the half-normal model without adjustments, yet there was a warning of high correlation between parameter estimates for that model.  Usually in that circumstance, AIC would favour the simpler model.  The high correlation is no doubt what caused the convergence failure when you tried using the R package.  (It also explains the very poor precision for this model reported in the book.)  But it seems that you get a better AIC for the model without adjustments using the R package.  That suggests to me that the fit of the half-normal without adjustments when using the Distance interface has failed to converge, even though it reports that it did converge.

 

It is very rare for the half-normal model to have convergence problems of this type, but I suspect that this is the issue here, rather than you doing anything wrong.

 

Steve Buckland

On Thursday, November 5, 2015 at 11:08:50 AM UTC-6, Stephen Buckland wrote:

That’s interesting.  I did the Montrave analyses for the book using the Distance software interface.  I was not comfortable with estimation using the half-normal model.  In my analyses, AIC selected one HP adjustment narrowly over the half-normal model without adjustments, yet there was a warning of high correlation between parameter estimates for that model.  Usually in that circumstance, AIC would favour the simpler model.  The high correlation is no doubt what caused the convergence failure when you tried using the R package.  (It also explains the very poor precision for this model reported in the book.)  But it seems that you get a better AIC for the model without adjustments using the R package.  That suggests to me that the fit of the half-normal without adjustments when using the Distance interface has failed to converge, even though it reports that it did converge.

 

It is very rare for the half-normal model to have convergence problems of this type, but I suspect that this is the issue here, rather than you doing anything wrong.

 

Steve Buckland

Subject: [distance-sampling] Montrave point dataset error in half-normal key function detection model

 

Hello,

I've been working with the point count example of the Montrave dataset for a couple of days now. Admittedly my experience with R is limited to simple analyses, but I do want to become more proficient with it so I'm trying to learn to analyze VCP data for the first time using the R Distance package instead of the Distance software interface. I am embarrassed by how long it has taken me to work with the example dataset being that you all have provided a link to the code, but nonetheless I have one issue I still cannot figure out. I'm getting an error when running the half-normal key function:

Starting AIC adjustment term selection.
Fitting half-normal key function
Key only models do not require monotonicity contraints. Not constraining model for monotonicity.
AIC= 444.782
Fitting half-normal key function with Hermite(4) adjustments
AIC= 444.524
Fitting half-normal key function with Hermite(4,6) adjustments


Error in model fitting, returning: half-normal key function with Hermite(4) adjustments

  Error: Error in detfct.fit.opt(ddfobj, optim.options, bounds, misc.options) :
  No convergence.

The uniform and hazard-rate key functions worked fine. Is this something I should be worried about? Or, just an additional sign that I do not want to select the half-normal key function? I could not find any mention of this in the Montrave case study document or Buckland et al. 2015, so I'm guessing I may have done something wrong?

Also, the results I get are different from those provided in Table 5.5 in Buckland et al. 2015. Delta AICs for uniform and half-normal compared to hazard-rate are 2.68 and 0.75, respectively and model results are:

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Montrave point dataset error in half-normal key function detection model
parts:
Lani

I can confirm that re-running the Montrave robin point count analysis repeatedly, the half-normal detection function, given an option to include Hermite adjustment terms, almost invariably chooses the half-normal with no adjustment terms.  Under that situation, the AIC is as you report, 444.78, and the estimate of robin density is 0.786 as reported in the online analysis report.

There are occasions where a 1 adjustment term Hermite is fitted to the robin data; none of my attempts resulted in an adjustment term model with a lower AIC than the no adjustment term model, as you report.  However there were numerous attempts where the adjustment term model failed to converge.  This supports Prof. Buckland's contention that the anomaly you reported was a result of convergence failure rather than coding errors on your part.

That’s interesting.  I did the Montrave analyses for the book using the Distance software interface.  I was not comfortable with estimation using the half-normal model.  In my analyses, AIC selected one HP adjustment narrowly over the half-normal model without adjustments, yet there was a warning of high correlation between parameter estimates for that model.  Usually in that circumstance, AIC would favour the simpler model.  The high correlation is no doubt what caused the convergence failure when you tried using the R package.  (It also explains the very poor precision for this model reported in the book.)  But it seems that you get a better AIC for the model without adjustments using the R package.  That suggests to me that the fit of the half-normal without adjustments when using the Distance interface has failed to converge, even though it reports that it did converge.

 

It is very rare for the half-normal model to have convergence problems of this type, but I suspect that this is the issue here, rather than you doing anything wrong.

 

Steve Buckland
